claims.text: The starting material is an FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy protective coating.
The starting coating has an as-cast microstructure containing randomly dispersed precipitates without long-range alignment.
Elevated-temperature exposure under sustained stress can promote precipitate raft formation.
The treatment produces a continuous, load-bearing precipitate raft structure.
A positive matrix–precipitate misfit promotes formation of a parallel precipitate raft microstructure during creep.
The precipitate raft structure stabilizes the microstructure.
The rafted precipitate network impedes dislocation movement.
The rafted precipitate network reorganizes internal stress distributions.
Impeded dislocation movement and reorganized internal stresses slow creep deformation relative to a non-rafted microstructure.
The raft-promoting treatment will reduce creep rate relative to an untreated as-cast control under identical sustained-stress conditions.
The raft-promoting treatment will delay the onset of tertiary creep relative to the untreated control.
The proposed mechanism is effective within the alloy's typical high-temperature operating range.
The mechanism may fail above the material's designed temperature or stress limits because of rapid microstructural degradation or phase changes.
A high-entropy superalloy with an FCC matrix and L12 ordered precipitates exhibited creep resistance at 982 °C comparable to some Ni-based superalloys.
The cited high-entropy superalloy formed parallel rafts during creep at 982 °C as a result of positive matrix–precipitate misfit.
The cited high-entropy superalloy's creep curves were dominated by tertiary creep.
Two groups will be compared: a stress-assisted thermally treated group and an untreated as-cast control.
Creep strain, precipitate morphology, and tertiary-creep onset will be measured during long-term constant-load testing.
The hypothesis is falsified if the treated group shows neither a statistically significant creep-rate reduction nor delayed tertiary-creep onset, or if a continuous raft structure is not observed.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts delayed tertiary creep due to rafting, whereas the only cited study reports that the raft-forming alloy's creep curves were dominated by tertiary creep. This does not directly disprove the prediction, but the evidence does not support the claimed delay.
